questions.q: How many hyperconjugative structures can be written for the isopropyl cation, (CH₃)₂CH⁺?
questions.explain: The number of hyperconjugative structures equals the number of α-hydrogens; the two methyl groups supply 6.

questions.q: According to the Baker–Nathan effect, the order of electron release by hyperconjugation from para alkyl groups is
options: All four groups release electrons equally
questions.explain: Hyperconjugation depends on the number of α-H atoms (3, 2, 1, 0), so methyl is highest. The first option is the +I order, the usual trap.

questions.q: Which alkene has the smallest heat of hydrogenation?
questions.explain: The tetrasubstituted alkene has 12 α-hydrogens and the most σ(C–H)→π* overlap, so it is the most stable and releases the least heat on hydrogenation (about −110 kJ/mol).

questions.q: The CH₃–C single bond in propyne is about 1.46 Å, shorter than the usual C–C bond of 1.54 Å. The best explanation is
options: The +I effect of the methyl group
The electromeric effect of the triple bond
Hyperconjugation, which gives the C–C bond partial double-bond character
Steric repulsion between the methyl hydrogens
questions.explain: σ(C–H) electrons of the methyl group delocalise into the adjacent π system, giving the CH₃–C bond some double-bond character and shortening it; the triple bond gains slight single-bond character.
